follows: fit_v2 (25 prompts per lens; UNVERIFIED): J++ macro pass@10 chat .706 vs wiki_a .638 (+.068 [+.03, +.11], led by poetry +.25), while the pooled lens was lower on chat (-.062 [-.09, -.03])
question: Does the chat pool's J++ advantage over WikiText hold at the recipe's 64 fitting prompts, and does our pipeline reproduce the published 64-prompt J++?
why: The human (Zach, 2026-10-17) asked for a chat fit on 64 prompts. The agent proposed adding wiki64: the published Qwen J++ was fitted by the J++ authors' own code (its config.yaml: source koayon/jpp-lenses, fitted 2026-09-07), so it is not a same-pipeline baseline. The human chose chat64 + wiki64 over chat64 alone.

chat64.fit_prompts: the pool's first 64 texts (fit_v2's 25-prompt lens used the first 25 of them)
chat64.router: cache/exp19/fit_v2/chat/router.pt copied (fit on the same pool's first 1000 texts, seed 0)

wiki64.fit_prompts: the pool's first 64 texts (fit_v2's 25-prompt lens used the first 25 of them)
wiki64.router: cache/exp19/fit_v2/wiki_a/router.pt copied (fit on the same pool's first 1000 texts, seed 0)

fit: fit_v2's recipe (rlens LRP, 16 Jacobian rows per pass, layers 0-62, expert weights on fit:0) with 64 shard prompts instead of 25; the router and the item grades are fit_v2's, so a 25-vs-64 comparison differs only in the number of shard prompts

evals.primary: jpp_cli.py evaluate (J++ readout evals, held-out:0), one call per condition right after its lenses are saved (J++ and pooled), in results/exp19_fit_data/RUN/eval_<condition>/
evals.combined_with: results/exp19_fit_data/fit_v2/eval_ranks.csv (the 25-prompt lenses, the published J++ and J-lens, logit). Pooling the files is valid because evaluate is deterministic: fit_v2's early and final evals gave identical ranks on all 231,525 shared rows
evals.analysis: scripts/exp19_fit_data/analyze.py (paired bootstrap over items, 10,000 resamples, seed 0)

decision.main: jpp_chat64 - jpp_wiki64, macro pass@10: the chat advantage holds at 64 prompts if the 95% CI excludes 0 on the positive side
decision.prediction: positive for J++ (led by poetry, as fit_v2); negative for the pooled lenses
decision.pipeline_check: jpp_wiki64 - published J++, macro pass@10: our pipeline reproduces the published fit if the CI includes 0; if not, the published lens is not a fair reference and fit_v2's 25-prompt cost (-.076, wiki_a vs published) mixes prompt count with pipeline
decision.scaling: chat64 - chat and wiki64 - wiki_a (64 vs 25 prompts within our pipeline), reported

limits: one fit per condition and no noise floor between fits (fit_v2's wiki_b was cancelled); each 64-prompt lens shares its first 25 prompts and its router with the fit_v2 lens of the same pool, so 25-vs-64 comparisons are not independent
